sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Pickaway County
sections.html:
The Pickaway County Recorder's Office is at 110 Island Road, Suite G, Circleville, Ohio 43113, inside the Pickaway County Service Center. The phone number is (740) 474-5826.

Land records here go back to the county's start in 1810. The office keeps a clear record of deeds, mortgages, easements, plats, land surveys, powers of attorney, leases and the liens that can attach to real estate. Staff do not prepare documents and cannot say whether a title is clear.

Mind the clock. Since April 1, 2025, documents brought in after 3:30 p.m. are not recorded until the first thing on the next business day. Staff still review them and check the fees at the counter.

Mail works only for originals that do not need approval stamps. The Engineer Map Department and the Auditor will not accept documents through the mail, and the recorder cannot route them for you. A deed that needs those stamps has to be carried in, and so does a transfer on death designation.

E-recording has been available since 2017 through a third-party vendor that the submitter chooses. Files can be sent any day, and staff process them from 8:00 a.m. to 3:45 p.m. on business days. A document with a new survey or new legal description cannot be e-recorded and must be walked through in person.

  • Bring or mail the original with a self-addressed, stamped envelope.
  • Pay by cash, check or card. A card payment adds $1.00 or 3%, whichever is greater.
  • If a deed was signed electronically and then printed, attach a separate authenticator certificate.

The base price follows the state schedule in Revised Code 317.32: $34 for the first two pages and $8 for each page after that, split between a base fee and a housing trust fund fee. Pickaway County adds the optional preservation surcharge. Since January 1, 2025, basic recording fees include $5.00 per document, which goes into the county general fund for preservation and digitization of records.

sections.h2: What the auditor requires before a transfer
sections.html:
The auditor's conveyance fee is $3.00 per thousand, for real estate and manufactured homes. State law puts it on the seller, and the auditor will not transfer an instrument without a completed DTE 100 or DTE 100EX form.

The county's Transfer and Conveyance Standards, set by the auditor and engineer under section 319.203, add more requirements:

  • The deed carries the original signature of the grantor and cannot be a fax or a copy.
  • It shows the auditor's parcel number, the site address, the prior deed reference and the grantee's tax mailing address.
  • A grantor who is not the prior grantee needs an explanation in the deed or an affidavit.
  • A new legal description needs the Engineer's Tax Map Department to stamp it "Mathematically Approved" first.
  • A split leaving a parcel of 20 acres or less needs planning commission approval.
  • A trust conveying property files an affidavit under section 5302.171 before or with the deed.

The recorder's online search runs on a site called CountyFusion. Name indexes cover 1/1/1990 to the present, historical indexes cover 1810 to 1990, and most images go back to 1980. Official Records began on April 16, 1996, and earlier records sit in separate books for deeds, mortgages, leases and other types.

You need a name to search. With only an address, look up the owner on the auditor's website first. Images found online can be downloaded and printed for free, and older documents can be ordered by volume and page for $2.00 a page.

The office also runs a free alert called FRAUDSLEUTH, which warns you when a document is recorded under names you enter. Sheriff's sale lists are kept on the sheriff's website, not the recorder's.

A paid-off mortgage shows up as a recorded release. The lender sends a Release of Mortgage, which is linked to the original mortgage in the records, and a copy is free on the recording site or from the office.

The bank does not hold your deed while you owe on the loan, and neither does the recorder, unlike a car title. You should have received the original after closing, and the office can copy a recorded deed if yours is lost.

To change the tax mailing address, call the Pickaway County Treasurer at (740) 474-2370. Changing the name on a deed requires a new deed prepared by an attorney.

The 2025 population estimate is 62,978, up 7.6% from the April 2020 base, with 23,832 housing units. Owners occupy 74.0% of homes, the median owner-occupied value is $256,800 and median gross rent is $1,020. New construction is active, with 406 building permits in 2025.

sections.h2: Selling acreage and watching for fraud
sections.html:
Many sales here involve acreage, so the land-split and survey rules above matter. For property maps outside a recorded subdivision, the recorder points owners to the Engineer's mapping department or GIS.

The recorder's page also carries an alert about Homeowner Benefit Agreements with MV Realty of Ohio. If you ever signed such an agreement, ask the recorder what is recorded against your parcel before you list, since anything on the record will come up in the title search.

sections.h2: Checklist before you hand in a deed
sections.html:
Run through this list before a sale closes, and most rejections go away.

  1. Confirm the grantor's original ink signature, not a copy.
  2. Confirm the parcel number, site address, prior deed reference and buyer's tax mailing address are on the deed.
  3. Get the Engineer's stamp first if there is a new legal description.
  4. Bring a completed DTE 100 or DTE 100EX for the auditor, and the conveyance fee at $3.00 per thousand.
  5. Arrive before 3:30 p.m. if you want it recorded the same day.

A cash sale does not change these steps, but it removes a buyer's lender from the timeline, so the deed is often ready sooner. Whichever way you sell, the recorder will not search your title, so a title company or examiner should confirm there are no open liens or unreleased mortgages before the deed is signed. Ask the closing agent to send you a copy of the recorded deed once it posts, and keep it with your sale papers. Cash Home Buyers CA can help you line up the paperwork.

faqs.q: What time must I bring a document to the recorder?
faqs.a: Before 3:30 p.m. if you want it recorded that day. Later arrivals are reviewed but not processed until the first thing the next business day.

faqs.q: Can a transfer on death designation be mailed in?
faqs.a: No. Documents that need the Engineer Map Department and Auditor stamps cannot be mailed, and transfer on death designations fall in that group.

faqs.q: How much is the conveyance fee in Pickaway County?
faqs.a: The auditor charges $3.00 per thousand, for both real estate and manufactured homes.

faqs.q: How do I get a copy of my recorded deed?
faqs.a: Download it free from the recorder's online site if it was recorded within the digital image coverage, or request a copy by phone, email, mail or in person at $2.00 a page.

faqs.q: Does the recorder search my title for liens?
faqs.a: No. Staff will show you how to search the records, but cannot say whether title is clear. Use a title examiner or title company for a full exam.
